newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberdrola sees 1997 earnings 95-100 bln pta.
newsitem.headline: Iberdrola sees 1997 earnings 95-100 bln pta.

text.p: Spanish electricity firm Iberdrola should see 1997 earnings of between 95 and 100 billion pesetas, financial director Jose Luis San Pedro said on Monday.
"I think that between 95 and 100 billion (pesetas) in 1997 is a target which is achievable and reasonable," he told journalists at a meeting.
He also said the firm was planning a further one percent cancellation of treasury stock this year, in line with a plan to cut treasury stock by up to five percent, as announced last May.
San Pedro said 1996 had been a record year, and this year's profit forecast was consistent with expected earnings growth of six to nine percent for the rest of the electricity sector.
Iberdrola's net profit in 1996 was 96 billion pesetas.
The firm has agreed a strategy to increase its dividend per share by less than earnings per share growth until the payout declines to 50 percent, he said.
The payout will fall to roughly 60 percent after a dividend paid against 1996 results, he said, versus around 71 percent in 1995.
Iberdrola is continuing a plan which will eventually reduce its workforce to 10,500 from around 12,100 in 1996.
San Pedro said the firm was unlikely to provision more against reserves to pay for worker retirements this year.
"1996 was probably the last year in which we have offset the cost of reducing personnel against profit," he said.
Future investment would depend heavily on what is decided by the government regarding national coal subsidies.

"The future of sector investment in Spain will depend greatly on the national coal plan...If large amounts of guaranteed coal production emerge (from the plan), there's no room (for new investment)" San Pedro said.
But, he added, "our idea this year is to intensify our investments fundamentally in Latin America."
